Unit 1: Let's Have Fun • Class 5 English (New NEP 2020)

Chapter 1: Papa's Spectacles

Humorous poem about domestic misplacement, observational warmth & family care

📄 Open Standalone Chapter Page (22 Questions) ↗
Chapter Highlights, Thematic Summary & Key Vocabulary
  • Themes of absent-mindedness, familial affection, and everyday domestic humor.
  • Papa frantically searches through coat pockets, chairs, and window sills, unaware the glasses rest on his own forehead.
  • Understanding empathy and the importance of lending a helpful, patient hand to elderly family members.
  • Vocabulary building: spectacles, chores, misplaced, frantic, perched, gratitude.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Comprehension (22 Solved Questions)
Q1 What is Papa searching for everywhere in the house? Let us Think • Comprehension 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Papa is frantically searching everywhere for his spectacles (reading glasses), without which he cannot read his morning newspaper or perform essential daily tasks.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Identification of spectacles / glasses 1 Mark
Explanation of urgency / daily reading necessity 1 Mark
Q2 Mention three possible places where Papa searched for his spectacles before discovering where they were. Let us Think • Comprehension 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Papa searched for his spectacles in: (1) Inside the deep pockets of his coats and shirts, (2) Underneath his favourite armchair and reading table, and (3) Along the window sill and bookshelves.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Inside pockets (coat/shirts) 1 Mark
Underneath chairs / furniture 1 Mark
Around window sills / shelves 1 Mark
Q3 At last, where does Papa find his lost item, and how does the narrator reveal it? Let us Think • Comprehension 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
At last, Papa discovers that his spectacles were perched safely right on top of his own head all along. The young narrator notices them and joyfully points out that he has been wearing them on his forehead the entire time.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Discovery location: on top of his head / forehead 1 Mark
Narrator's helpful and humorous revelation 1 Mark
Q4 Apart from reading the newspaper, what other household chores or activities would Papa find difficult to carry out without his spectacles? Let us Think • Think & Discuss 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Without his spectacles, Papa would struggle to: (1) Read fine print on medicine prescription bottles and food expiry labels, (2) Chop or slice vegetables safely in the kitchen, (3) Thread a sewing needle or write down domestic grocery lists, and (4) Operate dials on home appliances or view mobile messages clearly.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Reading medicine bottles / safety labels 1 Mark
Kitchen safety / chopping vegetables 1 Mark
Fine-detail vision tasks (threading / writing / screens) 1 Mark
Q5 What makes your papa happy, and how do you help elders at home when they misplace their everyday items? Let us Think • Think & Discuss 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
My papa feels happiest when the whole family sits together to share meals, when we share stories of our school day, and when the home is peaceful and orderly. Whenever an elder misplaces their keys or spectacles, I calmly retrace their steps, check their usual resting spots without panicking, and hand the item to them with a smile.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Things that bring happiness to elders / family togetherness 1.5 Marks
Constructive steps to help search calmly and respectfully 1.5 Marks
Q6 Identify four rhyming word pairs from the poem 'Papa's Spectacles' and frame one meaningful sentence with any one pair. Let us Learn • Vocabulary 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Rhyming Pairs from the Poem:
  • look — book
  • head — bed
  • chair — there
  • find — blind
Example Sentence: While sitting on the comfortable chair, grandfather was delighted to discover his notebook resting right there.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Listing 4 correct rhyming pairs (0.5 marks each) 2 Marks
Original, grammatically correct sentence using one pair 1 Mark
Q7 Complete the table: What things are commonly misplaced at home and at school, who helps locate them, and how should you express your gratitude? Let us Learn • Vocabulary 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
  • At Home:
    • Spectacles / Reading Glasses: Often misplaced on the dining table or sofa; located with Mother's or sibling's help.
    • House Keys / Mobile Phone: Slipped between couch cushions; located with Father's help.
  • At School:
    • Water Bottle / Pencil Box: Left behind near the playground bench or art room; located with Classmate's help.
    • Library Card / Notebook: Slipped inside the desk rack; located with Teacher's help.
  • Expressing Gratitude: Always say, "Thank you so much for taking time out to help me find this! I will keep it in its proper place now."
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Household items & helpers identified 1.5 Marks
School items & helpers identified 1.5 Marks
Polite expression of gratitude and responsibility 1 Mark
Q8 Rearrange the following jumbled words into grammatically correct sentences about Papa's search: Let us Learn • Grammar 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
  1. everywhere / searched / glasses / for / his / Papa
    → Papa searched everywhere for his glasses.
  2. resting / on / head / were / his / they
    → They were resting on his head.
  3. elders / should / patiently / help / we / our
    → We should patiently help our elders.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Sentence 1 correctly rearranged with capital letter & period 1 Mark
Sentence 2 correctly rearranged 1 Mark
Sentence 3 correctly rearranged 1 Mark
Q9 Write a short paragraph (5–6 sentences) describing a humorous domestic incident when a family member misplaced an everyday item. Let us Write • Creative Expression 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
The Great Remote Hunt:
Last Sunday, our entire living room turned into an archaeological dig when my elder brother could not find the television remote control just before the cricket match began. He checked under the sofa rugs, inside the refrigerator, and even accused our pet dog of burying it in the garden! Mother calmly walked into the room, smiled, and pointed to his left hand. Brother had been holding the remote control tightly the whole time while searching frantically with his right hand! We all burst into hearty laughter, and he sheepishly admitted how easily our eyes can play tricks on us.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Clear engaging narrative with humorous twist 2 Marks
Correct punctuation, tense consistency & descriptive vocabulary 2 Marks
Q10 Practical Exploration: Why do people need spectacles, and what are four essential daily habits to keep our eyes healthy? Let us Explore • Project Activity 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Why Spectacles are Needed: As people age or develop refractive errors (myopia or hypermetropia), the natural lens of the eye cannot focus light directly onto the retina, causing blurriness. Corrective lenses refract light so images appear crisp and clear.

Four Essential Eye Care Habits:
  1. Follow the 20-20-20 Rule: Every 20 minutes of screen reading, gaze at an object 20 feet away for 20 seconds to relax ciliary eye muscles.
  2. Read in Adequate Lighting: Never read books or mobile screens in dark rooms or under direct harsh glare.
  3. Eat Vitamin A-Rich Foods: Include carrots, spinach, papaya, and green leafy vegetables in your daily diet.
  4. Maintain Proper Posture: Hold books at least 25 to 30 centimeters away from your face while studying.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Scientific explanation of spectacle lenses 1 Mark
Four practical, age-appropriate eye health habits 2 Marks

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Observational Empathy & Elderly Support at Home

Case Scenario: During winter vacations, Rohan noticed his grandfather repeatedly squinting and rubbing his temples while trying to read the morning newspaper. Grandfather kept brushing it off, saying his glasses were just dirty, but Rohan noticed he held the paper unusually far away and struggled to read the dates on his medicine strips.

Question: Analyze Rohan's observation. What empathetic steps should Rohan take to ensure his grandfather receives proper care without feeling dependent or embarrassed?

Analysis & Actionable Empathy:
  1. Gentle Communication: Rohan should lovingly talk to his parents in private about his grandfather's visual strain rather than calling it out loudly in front of visitors.
  2. Arrange Professional Optometry: Request parents to schedule an eye checkup with an optometrist to update grandfather's reading prescription.
  3. Practical Daily Assistance: Offer to read aloud daily headlines and cross-check medicine dosages with a magnifying glass until new glasses arrive.
  4. Organized Storage: Gift grandfather a bright, designated spectacle case near his reading lamp so glasses are never misplaced again.
Rubric: 1.5 Marks for identifying presbyopia/eye strain + 3.5 Marks for 4 compassionate, dignified intervention steps = 5 Marks

Chapter 2: Gone with the Scooter

Lively neighborhood story about friendship, honesty, outdoor sports & an unexpected twist

📄 Open Standalone Chapter Page (22 Questions) ↗
Chapter Highlights, Thematic Summary & Key Vocabulary
  • Themes of honesty, ownership, cooperative neighborhood play, and resolving disputes calmly.
  • Gopi finds a lost ball in his garden and invites friends to play rather than selfishly hoarding it.
  • Friends (Deepak, Manoj, Ramani) argue over whose ball it might be before deciding to play together.
  • The surprise ending: a stray shot lands in a passing scooter's basket, carrying the ball away amidst universal laughter.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Comprehension (22 Solved Questions)
Q1 What was Gopi doing on the veranda when the story begins? Let us Think • Comprehension 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Gopi was sitting peacefully on the veranda of his home on a warm afternoon, immersed in reading an interesting storybook.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Setting identified (sitting on the veranda) 1 Mark
Activity identified (reading a book) 1 Mark
Q2 What unexpected sounds did Gopi hear before he walked into the garden? Let us Think • Comprehension 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Gopi suddenly heard a soft rustling sound amidst the dry leaves followed immediately by a distinct, heavy 'thud' in the garden.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Identified soft rustling sound 1 Mark
Identified heavy thud sound 1 Mark
Q3 Describe in detail Gopi's search for the mysterious object in his garden. Let us Think • Comprehension 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Gopi put down his book, stepped down into the garden, and walked toward the boundary fence. He parted the tall green grass, inspected the flowering bushes, and finally spotted a sturdy hockey ball resting snugly beneath a pile of dry autumn leaves.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Approaching boundary fence / tall grass 1 Mark
Inspecting bushes / foliage 1 Mark
Discovering hockey ball under dry leaves 1 Mark
Q4 Complete the table: Who said the following dialogues, and to whom were they spoken? Let us Think • Comprehension 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
  • a. "The ball I found is a hockey ball." → Said by Gopi to his friends (Deepak, Manoj, and Ramani).
  • b. "My father bought me a brand-new football." → Said by Deepak to Gopi and the friends.
  • c. "I lost a ball four months ago." → Said by Manoj to Gopi and the group.
  • d. "Show me the ball and I will tell you." → Said by Ramani to Gopi.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Statement (a) speaker and listener correctly identified 1 Mark
Statement (b) speaker and listener correctly identified 1 Mark
Statement (c) speaker and listener correctly identified 1 Mark
Statement (d) speaker and listener correctly identified 1 Mark
Q5 Who grabbed the ball from Gopi, and how did their street game begin? Let us Think • Comprehension 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Manoj grabbed the ball from Gopi's hands. Recognizing that arguing over ownership was pointless, Gopi stepped into the center with his hockey stick, passed the ball to Deepak, Deepak dribbled and flicked it toward Ramani, and a lively neighborhood game commenced.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Manoj identified as grabbing the ball 1 Mark
Transition from dispute to cooperative play 1 Mark
Passing and dribbling between Gopi, Deepak, and Ramani 1 Mark
Q6 Why did all the children burst into laughter at the conclusion of the story? Let us Think • Comprehension 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
During the game, a vigorous shot struck the ball high into the air. It landed perfectly inside the front wire basket of a passing scooter! The scooterist sped away unaware, leaving the children empty-handed but thoroughly amused at the hilarious coincidence.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Ball landing in the passing scooter's basket 1 Mark
Scooter driving away causing humorous climax 1 Mark
Q7 What would you have done if, like Gopi, you found a ball or valuable toy in your garden that did not belong to you? Let us Think • Think & Discuss 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
If I found a lost ball or toy, I would first check with immediate neighbors and children playing nearby to see if anyone lost it recently. If no owner stepped forward, I would keep it safely and invite neighborhood friends to play with it together, ensuring honesty and community spirit rather than fighting over ownership.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Checking with neighbors / nearby children honestly 1.5 Marks
Constructive sharing / safe custody 1.5 Marks
Q8 Match the following vocabulary words from 'Gone with the Scooter' to their exact definitions: Let us Learn • Vocabulary 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
  • Dribble: Moving a ball forward with gentle, controlled taps using a stick or feet.
  • Boast: Speaking excessively proudly or bragging about one's possessions or skills.
  • Rustle: A soft, crisp crackling sound produced by dry leaves or paper rubbing together.
  • Grab: To seize or take hold of something suddenly with a quick, firm motion.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Dribble definition matched 1 Mark
Boast definition matched 1 Mark
Rustle definition matched 1 Mark
Grab definition matched 1 Mark
Q9 Fill in the blanks using suitable Collective Nouns and Sports Action Verbs: Let us Learn • Grammar 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
  1. A team of young players gathered in the lane to play hockey.
  2. Gopi watched the ball dribble across the grassy lawn.
  3. A cheerful crowd of neighbors watched the children play from their balconies.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Blank 1: 'team' identified correctly 1 Mark
Blank 2: 'dribble' / action verb identified 1 Mark
Blank 3: 'crowd' / collective noun identified 1 Mark
Q10 Discussion Prompt: Why is outdoor neighborhood play vital for children, and how does it teach conflict resolution? Let us Speak & Listen 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Key Discussion Points:
  • Physical Fitness: Running, bending, and striking improve cardiovascular stamina, agility, and motor reflexes far more than video games.
  • Conflict Resolution: In the story, rather than shouting over who owns the ball, the boys channel their energy into playing together. Outdoor play teaches negotiation, compromise, and rule-following.
  • Social Bonding: Playing on the street creates enduring friendships, teaches gracious winning and losing, and nurtures empathy.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Physical health benefits highlighted 1 Mark
Conflict resolution & negotiation skills explained 1 Mark
Social development & sportsmanship described 1 Mark
Q11 Create a Sports Inventory Chart: List 5 ball games, stating the ball type, number of players, and core rule for each. Let us Explore • Project Activity 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
  • 1. Cricket: Hard leather/cork ball; 11 players per side; batting team scores runs while fielding team attempts dismissals.
  • 2. Football: Stitched leather sphere; 11 players per side; players kick the ball into opponent's goal without using hands (except goalkeeper).
  • 3. Field Hockey: Hard plastic/composite dimpled ball; 11 players per side; curved sticks maneuver the ball into goal nets.
  • 4. Basketball: Large inflated rubber/leather ball; 5 players on court; bouncing/dribbling ball to shoot through an elevated ring.
  • 5. Tennis: Hollow rubber felt-coated ball; 1 (singles) or 2 (doubles); rackets volley the ball over a center net within boundary lines.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
5 distinct ball sports listed accurately 2 Marks
Equipment, team size, and core rule documented for each 2 Marks

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Integrity, Sharing & Peaceful Conflict Management

Case Scenario: During recess, Kabir finds an expensive imported badminton racket lying unattended on the bleachers. Two classmates, Aman and Tushar, immediately rush over. Aman claims his cousin owns an identical one, while Tushar insists whoever picked it up has the right to keep it or trade it.

Question: Drawing inspiration from Gopi's ethical handling in 'Gone with the Scooter', outline the steps Kabir should take to ensure honesty and fairness prevail.

Action Plan for Ethical Conflict Resolution:
  1. Reject 'Finders Keepers': Kabir must firmly explain that finding an unattended object does not confer legal or moral ownership. Keeping it would amount to dishonesty.
  2. Deposit with Authority: Hand the racket over immediately to the Physical Education teacher or school Lost and Found desk, noting the time and location found.
  3. Public Announcement: Request the teacher to make an announcement asking the rightful owner to identify the racket by describing specific marks or brand details.
  4. Promote Cooperative Sportsmanship: Suggest that while awaiting the owner, the friends can borrow standard school equipment to play doubles together, avoiding personal disputes.
Rubric: 1.5 Marks for ethical rejection of false ownership + 3.5 Marks for 4 structured conflict-resolution steps = 5 Marks

Chapter 3: The Rainbow

Christina Rossetti's lyrical poem celebrating natural beauty over human engineering

📄 Open Standalone Chapter Page (22 Questions) ↗
Chapter Highlights, Thematic Summary & Key Vocabulary
  • Themes of nature's sublime grandeur, poetic comparison, and the wonder of rainbows.
  • Contrasting human inventions (boats, ships, river bridges) with celestial natural wonders (clouds sailing in the sky, rainbow bridging heaven).
  • Poetic devices: imagery, personification, symbolism of the arch from earth to sky.
  • Vocabulary building: sail, o'ertops, bow, bridges, heaven, prettier.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Comprehension (22 Solved Questions)
Q1 Explain the meaning and imagery of the word 'bow' as used in Christina Rossetti's poem. Let us Think • Comprehension 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
In the poem, the word 'bow' refers to the rainbow. It describes the magnificent multicolored arch or curved bow that spans across the sky after rainfall, symbolizing a celestial bridge connecting heaven and earth.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Identification of 'bow' as rainbow 1 Mark
Explanation of curved arch connecting earth and sky 1 Mark
Q2 Which bridge does the poet admire more than man-made river bridges, and why? Let us Think • Comprehension 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
The poet admires the rainbow—the bow that bridges heaven—far more than human-built river bridges. She explains that while river bridges are useful and pretty, the rainbow is 'prettier far than these' because it overtops tallest trees and builds a magical celestial road from earth to the sky.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Identified rainbow as the preferred bridge 1 Mark
Textual quote: 'prettier far than these' 1 Mark
Reason: overtops trees / builds road to sky 1 Mark
Q3 The word 'these' appears in both stanzas. What specific objects does 'these' refer to in each stanza? Let us Think • Comprehension 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
In stanza one, 'these' refers to the boats sailing on rivers and ships sailing on seas. In stanza two, 'these' refers to the man-made stone and wooden bridges built across rivers.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Stanza 1: 'these' = boats and ships 1 Mark
Stanza 2: 'these' = bridges on rivers 1 Mark
Q4 State whether the following statements are True or False according to the poem: Let us Think • Comprehension 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
  1. Ships sail on the river. → False. (The poem states boats sail on rivers, while ships sail on seas).
  2. Boats sail on the sea. → False. (The poem states ships sail on seas, while boats sail on rivers).
  3. Bridges are built on the river. → True. (The poem notes there are bridges on rivers, pretty as you please).
  4. A road is built from earth to the sky. → True (Poetically). (The poem states the rainbow 'builds a road from earth to sky').
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Statement (a) identified as False with reason 1 Mark
Statement (b) identified as False with reason 1 Mark
Statement (c) identified as True 1 Mark
Statement (d) identified as True / Poetic truth 1 Mark
Q5 What are the various ways humans cross rivers, and how do bridges help communities prosper? Let us Think • Think & Discuss 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Humans cross rivers using wooden boats, motor ferries, bamboo rafts, suspended cable cars, and permanent bridges (suspension, arch, or girder bridges). Bridges connect isolated villages to markets, schools, and hospitals, enabling seamless trade, transit, and emergency healthcare.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Listing diverse river crossing methods (boats/ferries/bridges) 1.5 Marks
Socio-economic impact of bridges on community development 1.5 Marks
Q6 Have you ever observed a rainbow in nature? Describe what atmospheric conditions cause it and how you felt looking at it. Let us Think • Think & Discuss 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Yes, I saw a vibrant rainbow arching across the horizon after a gentle monsoon drizzle when the sun broke through the clouds. A rainbow occurs when sunlight passes through millions of falling raindrops, which act as tiny prisms, refracting, reflecting, and dispersing white light into its seven constituent colors. Seeing it filled me with wonder and serenity.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Personal observation described with emotional impact 1.5 Marks
Scientific atmospheric condition (sunlight + rain droplets refracting light) 1.5 Marks
Q7 Complete the table of Degrees of Comparison for adjectives featured in and inspired by the poem: Let us Learn • Vocabulary 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
  • Positive: Pretty  |  Comparative: Prettier  |  Superlative: Prettiest
  • Positive: High  |  Comparative: Higher  |  Superlative: Highest
  • Positive: Great  |  Comparative: Greater  |  Superlative: Greatest
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme

High / Higher / Highest correct 1 Mark

Q8 Explain the scientific acronym VIBGYOR and write a memorable mnemonic sentence to remember the colors in correct sequence. Let us Learn • Vocabulary 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
VIBGYOR Sequence:
  • V: Violet
  • I: Indigo
  • B: Blue
  • G: Green
  • Y: Yellow
  • O: Orange
  • R: Red
Popular Mnemonic: "Richard Of York Gave Battle In Vain" (Reversed) or "Very Intelligent Boys Give Young Old Respect".
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
All 7 rainbow colors listed in precise optical order 2 Marks
Creative, correct mnemonic sentence provided 1 Mark
Q9 Write a short descriptive paragraph (50–60 words) capturing the sights, scents, and sounds of a countryside after a fresh rainfall. Let us Write • Descriptive Writing 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Nature's Fresh Canvas:
As the dark thunderclouds parted, a warm golden ray of sunlight bathed the countryside. The soothing scent of wet earth (petrichor) rose from the soil. Crystal raindrops glistened like diamonds on trembling green leaves. Birds chirped enthusiastically from tree branches, and across the eastern sky stretched a majestic, luminous rainbow that made the whole world look washed, renewed, and joyful.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Rich sensory details (petrichor, glistening drops, birdsong) 2 Marks
Accurate grammar, spelling, and expressive vocabulary 2 Marks
Q10 Step-by-Step Practical Activity: How can you create a miniature rainbow in your classroom or home using water and sunlight? Let us Explore • Science Experiment 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Materials Needed: A shallow glass bowl of water, a small flat mirror, a white sheet of cardboard, and bright sunlight.

Procedure:
  1. Place the glass bowl of water near a sunny window with direct sunlight falling into it.
  2. Submerge the flat mirror inside the water at a tilted angle (around 45 degrees).
  3. Position the white cardboard sheet in the shade opposite the mirror.
  4. Adjust the angle until the reflected beam strikes the white cardboard, revealing a spectrum of seven vibrant rainbow colors!
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Clear listing of accessible materials 1 Mark
Accurate step-by-step optical dispersion procedure 2 Marks

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Artistic Appreciation & Environmental Stewardship

Case Scenario: A town municipal corporation plans to build a six-lane concrete flyover through an ancient city park, arguing that roads symbolize human progress. School students argue that cutting down century-old banyan trees will permanently destroy the green canopy where clouds, birds, and natural beauty thrive.

Question: Connecting this dilemma to Christina Rossetti's theme in 'The Rainbow', formulate three compelling arguments the students should submit to urge the city to adopt eco-sensitive green architecture.

Eco-Sensitive Architecture Proposals:
  1. Inherent Superiority of Natural Systems: Just as Rossetti shows that clouds and rainbows surpass stone bridges in beauty, mature urban trees provide vital ecological services (air purification, temperature cooling, bird nesting) that no concrete flyover can replicate.
  2. Subterranean or Elevated Bypass Alignment: Re-route the flyover around the perimeter of the heritage park or construct a tunneled bypass to preserve 100% of the forest canopy intact.
  3. Green Canopy Bridges & Eco-Ducts: If road expansion is inevitable, mandate wildlife-friendly overpasses lined with native plants to maintain natural continuity between disjointed green pockets.
Rubric: 1.5 Marks for thematic connection to Rossetti's nature vs. engineering motif + 3.5 Marks for 3 actionable eco-urban planning solutions = 5 Marks

Chapter 4: The Wise Parrot

Panchatantra-style fable illustrating that wisdom and intellect surpass brute strength

📄 Open Standalone Chapter Page (22 Questions) ↗
Chapter Highlights, Thematic Summary & Key Vocabulary
  • Themes of true freedom vs. gilded captivity, clever wit, and animal welfare.
  • A wealthy merchant treats his pet parrot with luxury, but the bird yearns for natural forest freedom.
  • The message to wild parrots: a forest bird plays dead, silently communicating the secret escape technique.
  • The climax: the pet parrot feigns death on the windowsill and soars to liberation.
  • Grammar: simple past tense of irregular verbs, synonyms, and antonyms.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Comprehension (22 Solved Questions)
Q1 Why did the wealthy merchant keep the parrot inside a golden cage? Let us Think • Comprehension 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
The merchant kept the parrot in a golden cage because it was his most cherished pet. He wanted to provide it with luxury, protect it from predators, and keep its joyful songs and conversations close to him at all times.

Pet was deeply cherished / favorite companion 1 Mark
Desire to protect in luxury and enjoy its songs 1 Mark
Q2 What special qualities made the parrot the merchant's favorite pet? Let us Think • Comprehension 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
The parrot was exceptionally intelligent, lively, and articulate. It entertained the merchant with delightful songs, mimicked words, and recited captivating stories that cheered him up after long trading journeys.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
High intelligence and pleasant vocal mimicry 1 Mark
Storytelling and comforting companionship 1 Mark
Q3 What message did the parrot ask the merchant to convey to its wild companions in the forest? Let us Think • Comprehension 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Before the merchant embarked on his business journey to the forest, the parrot asked him to deliver its warm greetings to its fellow wild parrots and inform them that while it lived in a gilded cage with abundant food, it still deeply missed flying freely with them in the treetops.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Conveying warm greetings to forest companions 1 Mark
Describing life in the golden cage 1 Mark
Expressing longing for natural forest freedom 1 Mark
Q4 What unexpected event occurred when the merchant delivered the message to the forest parrots? Let us Think • Comprehension 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
When the merchant delivered the message in the deep woods, one of the wild parrots listened silently, stiffened its feathers, tumbled off the tree branch, and fell motionless to the ground, appearing completely lifeless. The merchant was shocked, believing his message had caused its death.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Wild parrot listening silently to message 1 Mark
Falling motionless from branch to ground 1 Mark
Merchant believing the bird had died of grief 1 Mark
Q5 How did the caged parrot escape from the merchant upon hearing the news? Let us Think • Comprehension 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Upon hearing the merchant recount the wild bird's fate, the pet parrot immediately understood the silent coded message. It dropped to the floor of its cage, stiffened its claws, and played dead. When the grieving merchant opened the door and placed the 'corpse' on the windowsill, the parrot instantly took wing and soared into the sky.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Decoding the silent signal to play dead 1 Mark
Merchant placing lifeless body on windowsill 1 Mark
Instant flight to natural freedom 1 Mark
Q6 If you were the merchant, how would you respond to the parrot's escape? Can true love exist without freedom? Let us Think • Think & Discuss 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Though I would feel a momentary pang of loneliness, I would ultimately feel happy for the parrot's freedom. True affection means wishing for the happiness and self-fulfillment of the other creature. Keeping an animal confined in a cage—no matter how lavish—is selfish; genuine love respects their natural right to fly free.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Mature emotional balance (accepting parting) 1.5 Marks
Philosophical insight: true love demands freedom, not possession 1.5 Marks
Q7 Describe a real-life situation where wisdom and intelligence proved far more effective than physical strength. Let us Think • Think & Discuss 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
When a puppy fell into a narrow open drainage pit in our neighborhood, several adults tried pulling the concrete slabs with crowbars but risked collapsing the walls onto the puppy. A smart schoolgirl tied a soft wicker basket to a strong rope, placed fresh biscuits inside, and gently lowered it. The puppy stepped inside to eat, and she smoothly pulled it up to safety without harm.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Vivid, realistic dilemma described 1.5 Marks
Demonstration of wit/technique outperforming brute force 1.5 Marks

Q10 Write a short dramatic dialogue (4–6 exchanges) between the parrot on the windowsill and the startled merchant before it flies away. Let us Write • Dialogue Writing 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Merchant: (Gasping in astonishment) "You were motionless a second ago! How can you be alive?"
Parrot: (Flapping its vibrant green wings) "My dear master, my friend in the forest sent me advice, not grief. He showed me that to escape captivity, one must appear lifeless!"
Merchant: (Softly) "I gave you a golden cage and sweet fruits. Were you not happy?"
Parrot: "A cage of gold is still a prison, master. The blue sky cannot be bought with golden bars. Thank you for your care, but I belong to the wind!"
Merchant: "Fly safe, wise friend. I understand now."
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Dramatic, expressive dialogue capturing core theme 2 Marks
Proper script formatting, stage directions & punctuation 2 Marks
Q11 Animal Welfare Project: Formulate three fundamental principles why birds should never be caged as pets. Let us Explore • Animal Welfare 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Three Principles for Avian Freedom:
  1. Biological Deprivation: Birds are anatomically designed for flight. Caging atrophies their wing muscles, causing severe physical suffering.
  2. Psychological Trauma: Highly social animals like parrots suffer depression, feather plucking, and distress when separated from natural flocks.
  3. Ecological Disruption: Wild birds play indispensable ecological roles as seed dispersers and forest regenerators that are nullified by pet trade capture.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Biological impact of flight restriction 1 Mark
Psychological trauma and distress in captivity 1 Mark
Ecological role in seed dispersal & pollination 1 Mark

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Critical Thinking & Non-Violent Strategic Communication

Case Scenario: During a school debate on animal rights, one team argues that keeping wild exotic birds in air-conditioned luxury enclosures is beneficial because it protects them from forest predators and natural food shortages.

Question: Drawing evidence from 'The Wise Parrot', refute this argument by proving why freedom and self-determination are fundamental rights that luxury cannot compensate for.

Rebuttal Based on 'The Wise Parrot':
  1. The Fallacy of Gilded Captivity: The merchant provided the finest golden cage and exotic seeds, yet the parrot risked death to escape. This proves that an animal's primary welfare need is bodily autonomy and the natural exercise of instincts, not artificial luxury.
  2. Predation vs. Confinement: While nature carries risks, wild ecosystems allow animals dignity, companionship, flight, and purpose. Confinement reduces living beings to decorative trophies for human amusement.
  3. The Ethics of Custody: True conservation focuses on preserving native wild habitats (forest reserves), not locking individuals in cages under the guise of protection.
Rubric: 1.5 Marks for refuting the 'safety in captivity' premise + 3.5 Marks for 3 philosophical & biological arguments based on textual evidence = 5 Marks

Unit 3: Water • Class 5 English (New NEP 2020)

Chapter 5: The Frog

Lively nature poem on amphibious adaptations, wetland ecosystems & biological wonder

📄 Open Standalone Chapter Page (22 Questions) ↗
Chapter Highlights, Thematic Summary & Key Vocabulary
  • Themes of amphibian life, unique physical adaptations, and predator-prey dynamics.
  • The dual habitat of the frog: thriving both on damp terrestrial soil and inside aquatic ponds.
  • Physical traits: webbed hind feet for swimming, powerful leaping legs, protective camouflage, lightning-fast tongue.
  • Grammar focus: coordinating conjunctions (and, but, because, so) and sentence unscrambling.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Comprehension (22 Solved Questions)
Q1 Where does the frog like to sit and spend its time according to the poem? Let us Think • Comprehension 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
The frog likes to sit comfortably in calm ponds, splash in the pouring rain, and hop through muddy ditches and damp garden drains.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Mentioning cool ponds / rain 1 Mark
Mentioning muddy drains / garden soil 1 Mark
Q2 Describe the specialized mechanism by which a frog captures its prey. Let us Think • Comprehension 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
The frog spots insects with its prominent bulging eyes and captures them by flicking out its long, sticky tongue with lightning-fast speed, snapping the prey into its mouth in the blink of an eye.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Use of long, sticky tongue 1 Mark
Lightning-fast flicking motion capturing insects 1 Mark
Q3 How does the frog move differently in water compared to its locomotion on land? Let us Think • Comprehension 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
In water, the frog swims effortlessly by kicking backwards with its webbed hind feet that function like boat oars. On land, it uses its muscular, folded hind legs to leap and hop high into the air across distances.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
In water: swimming with webbed feet pushing water 1.5 Marks
On land: hopping and leaping with powerful hind legs 1.5 Marks
Q4 What natural camouflage protects the frog from being spotted by predators? Let us Think • Comprehension 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
The frog's moist skin is patterned in shades of green, brown, and olive that perfectly match surrounding waterweeds, mud, and grass, making it nearly invisible to predatory snakes and birds.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Moist green and brown skin coloration 1 Mark
Blending with surrounding plants, grass, and mud 1 Mark
Q5 What would it feel like to live as an amphibian, capable of existing both in water and on land? Let us Think • Think & Discuss 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Living as an amphibian would be exciting because you could dive into cool water during scorching summer afternoons and leap onto land to sunbathe on lily pads. However, you would need to constantly keep your skin moist to breathe and stay vigilant against land and water predators.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Creative reflection on dual habitat life 1.5 Marks
Awareness of biological vulnerability (skin moisture, predators) 1.5 Marks
Q6 How are a frog's webbed feet analogous to the swim flippers used by scuba divers? Let us Think • Think & Discuss 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Both frog feet and scuba flippers have thin, flexible webbing connecting the toes/edges. By creating a wider surface area against the water, they displace more liquid with every kick, generating greater forward thrust with minimal energy expenditure.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Identification of thin webbing connecting toes/blades 1.5 Marks
Explanation of surface area displacement & forward propulsion 1.5 Marks
Q7 In what significant biological ways is a frog's life cycle different from that of a fish? Let us Think • Think & Discuss 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
A fish breathes with gills and remains entirely aquatic throughout its lifespan. A frog undergoes complete metamorphosis: it begins as a gilled, legless aquatic tadpole and transforms into an air-breathing, four-legged adult amphibian capable of hopping on land.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Fish: fully aquatic throughout life with gills 1.5 Marks
Frog: complete metamorphosis from aquatic tadpole to terrestrial adult 1.5 Marks

✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
  1. My colors match the surrounding plants and trees.
  2. Would you like to learn about frogs and tadpoles?
  3. I hop around happily, but I must watch out for hungry snakes!

Q9 Rearrange the jumbled words into meaningful sentences about animal adaptations: Let us Learn • Grammar 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
  1. water / through / webbed / cuts / feet / with / frog / the
    → The frog cuts through water with webbed feet.
  2. insects / tongue / its / catches / with / it / flying
    → It catches flying insects with its tongue.
  3. snakes / watchful / remains / of / it / always
    → It always remains watchful of snakes.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Sentence 1 rearranged accurately 1 Mark
Sentence 2 rearranged accurately 1 Mark
Sentence 3 rearranged accurately 1 Mark
Q10 Write an informative 5-sentence note on the four stages of a frog's metamorphosis. Let us Write • Informative Paragraph 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
The Wonder of Metamorphosis:
1. A mother frog lays clusters of jelly-coated eggs called frogspawn in calm pond water.
2. These eggs hatch into tiny, tail-swimming tadpoles that breathe through external gills and feed on algae.
3. Gradually, the tadpole sprouts back legs and front arms while its tail begins to shrink.
4. In the froglet stage, lungs develop as it prepares to leave the water.
5. Finally, the tail is fully absorbed, and an adult frog emerges ready to live both on land and in water.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
All 4 life stages (Egg, Tadpole, Froglet, Adult Frog) explained 2.5 Marks
Scientific accuracy, logical flow and correct vocabulary 1.5 Marks
Q11 Why are frogs considered essential 'bio-indicators' of a healthy freshwater environment? Let us Explore • Environmental Science 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Frogs as Environmental Guardians:
Frogs possess permeable, porous skin through which they absorb water and oxygen. Because their skin directly interacts with their surroundings, they are extremely sensitive to water pollution, chemical pesticides, and acid rain. If frogs disappear from a local pond or marshland, it serves as an immediate early warning to scientists that the water source is contaminated. Furthermore, by eating thousands of mosquitoes, frogs naturally prevent the spread of diseases like malaria and dengue.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Permeable skin sensitivity to water pollution explained 1.5 Marks
Mosquito control and disease prevention role highlighted 1.5 Marks

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Wetland Conservation & Bio-Indicator Science

Case Scenario: A residential developer plans to drain a natural municipal pond and fill it with rubble to construct a parking lot. Local children notice that the croaking of frogs, which used to be loud every monsoon, has completely silenced over the past two years due to plastic dumping in the pond.

Question: Apply your understanding of 'The Frog' to construct a 3-point petition explaining why draining this wetland will trigger ecological collapse and pest outbreaks in the neighborhood.

Student Environmental Petition Points:
  1. Natural Insect Population Control: Adult frogs consume enormous quantities of mosquito larvae, beetles, and flies daily. Destroying their wetland breeding ground will cause an explosion in disease-spreading mosquito populations across the residential colony.
  2. Disruption of the Food Chain: Frogs serve as an essential middle link in the local food web, sustaining herons, egrets, harmless garden snakes, and birds of prey. Losing them collapses local urban biodiversity.
  3. Natural Rainwater Retention: Wetlands act as nature's sponge during heavy rainfall, preventing urban street waterlogging and recharging groundwater tables for nearby tube-wells.
Rubric: 1.5 Marks for highlighting mosquito control & disease prevention + 3.5 Marks for food web & groundwater conservation arguments = 5 Marks

Chapter 6: What a Tank!

Cultural and architectural travelogue on Punjab's unique rooftop water tanks & water conservation

📄 Open Standalone Chapter Page (22 Questions) ↗
Chapter Highlights, Thematic Summary & Key Vocabulary
  • Themes of traditional water storage, creative community identity, and regional pride in Punjab.
  • The architectural marvel of Punjab's rooftop water tanks shaped as tractors, aeroplanes, birds, and sports gear.

📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Comprehension (22 Solved Questions)
Q1 What is the primary utility and purpose of an overhead water tank in domestic buildings? Let us Think • Comprehension 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
An overhead water tank stores water pumped from groundwater borewells or municipal supply lines, using natural gravitational pressure to distribute it smoothly across taps, kitchens, washrooms, and gardens without requiring continuous electric pumping.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Storage of water from municipal/groundwater sources 1 Mark
Use of gravity to provide smooth tap pressure 1 Mark
Q2 Where is the state of Punjab situated on the map of India, and what does its name signify? Let us Think • Comprehension 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Punjab is located in the northwestern region of India. Its name originates from two Persian words: 'Panj' (meaning five) and 'Aab' (meaning water), signifying the fertile 'Land of Five Rivers' (Sutlej, Beas, Ravi, Chenab, and Jhelum).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Geographic location: North-western India 1 Mark
Etymology: Land of Five Rivers 1 Mark
Q3 Describe the construction process and materials used to build artistic rooftop water tanks in Punjab. Let us Think • Comprehension 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Skilled local artisans first weld a sturdy structural frame using malleable steel rods and wire mesh in the shape of the desired object (tractor, plane, or horse). Concrete cement and waterproof mortar are then layered over the frame. Once cured, it is coated with vibrant waterproof paints, transforming a functional tank into durable rooftop art.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Steel rod and wire mesh skeleton framework 1 Mark
Concrete cement layering and waterproofing 1 Mark
Vibrant painting and final rooftop installation 1 Mark
Q4 How do the distinctive shapes of water tanks reflect the identity, achievements, and aspirations of homeowners? Let us Think • Comprehension 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Each sculpted tank tells a personal story: a farmer constructs a tractor-shaped tank celebrating agricultural prosperity; a family with relatives working abroad builds an aeroplane-shaped tank symbolizing international travel; an athlete chooses a football or weightlifter; while an army veteran displays a cannon or tank symbolizing national service.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Tractor = Agricultural prosperity / farming roots 1 Mark
Aeroplane = Global travel / diaspora pride 1 Mark
Sports / Military motifs = Personal passions and service 1 Mark
Q5 Apart from overhead tanks, identify and explain four diverse traditional and modern water conservation systems across India. Let us Think • Think & Discuss 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
  • 1. Baolis (Step-wells of Gujarat & Rajasthan): Deep architectural wells with stone steps descending to subterranean water tables.
  • 2. Tankas (Underground Cisterns of Thar): Covered circular chambers built in courtyards to harvest every drop of desert rainwater.
  • 3. Ooranis (Traditional Ponds of Tamil Nadu): Community percolation ponds designed to catch surface runoff and recharge village wells.
  • 4. Rooftop Rainwater Harvesting (Modern): Channeling roof runoff through sand-gravel filters directly into groundwater aquifers.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Baolis / step-wells explained 1 Mark
Tankas / underground cisterns explained 1 Mark
Ooranis / percolation ponds explained 1 Mark
Modern Rainwater Harvesting explained 1 Mark

The open book would symbolize the thirst for knowledge and wisdom that our school nurtures, while the green olive branch would remind every student that true education must protect the environment and save every drop of water.

Q10 Project Work: Describe the four essential stages of a household Rooftop Rainwater Harvesting (RWH) system. Let us Explore • Environmental Engineering 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Four Stages of Rooftop Rainwater Harvesting:
  1. Catchment Area (Rooftop): The clean roof surface that intercepts falling raindrops during monsoon storms.
  2. Conveyance Network (Gutters & Downpipes): UV-resistant PVC channels that transport rainwater downwards from roof slopes.
  3. Filtration Unit (First-Flush & Sand-Gravel Filter): A diverter discards the initial dirty water, followed by charcoal, sand, and gravel chambers that filter out dust and leaves.
  4. Storage Cistern / Aquifer Recharge Pit: Clean water is stored in sealed underground tanks or directed through perforated pipes into dry borewells to replenish the groundwater table.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Catchment & conveyance explained 2 Marks
Filtration and storage/recharge explained 2 Marks

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Cultural Heritage & Modern Sustainable Architecture

Case Scenario: A heritage tourist organization visits a rural cluster in Punjab and observes over 50 unique rooftop tanks. A visitor points out that while the decorative tanks look striking, several overflow during power pumping, wasting hundreds of liters of treated water daily.

Question: Propose three smart technological and civic solutions that preserve Punjab's artistic tank tradition while eliminating water wastage completely.

Smart & Sustainable Cultural Heritage Solutions:
  1. Automatic Smart Float Sensor Switches: Install low-cost automated magnetic sensors in every sculpted tank that automatically shut off the electric water pump the moment water reaches 95% capacity, ending overflow wastage.
  2. Overflow Recirculation Ducts: Retrofit an overflow return pipe that redirects accidental excess water down into a rainwater recharge pit or kitchen garden rather than splashing onto streets.
  3. Community Eco-Artisan Certification: Train local tank sculptors to integrate level gauges and overflow alarms as standard design specifications in every new sculpture they build.
Rubric: 1.5 Marks for balancing cultural aesthetics with conservation + 3.5 Marks for 3 smart engineering and civic recommendations = 5 Marks

Chapter 7: Gilli Danda

Rhythmic sports poem celebrating India's ancient street game, agile hand-eye coordination & outdoor joy

📄 Open Standalone Chapter Page (22 Questions) ↗
Chapter Highlights, Thematic Summary & Key Vocabulary
  • Themes of traditional outdoor play, indigenous Indian games, and joyous camaraderie.
  • The mechanics of Gilli Danda: a long wooden danda striking the tapered gilli into flight.
  • Health benefits of energetic open-air group sports versus isolated sedentary screen time.
  • Grammar focus: prefixes (un-, re-) to form antonyms and absolute possessive pronouns.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Comprehension (22 Solved Questions)
Q1 Which indigenous sport does the poem celebrate, and what two items of wooden equipment are needed to play it? Let us Think • Comprehension 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
The poem celebrates the ancient traditional Indian sport of Gilli Danda. The equipment required comprises: (1) A danda (a long, sturdy wooden stick roughly two feet long) and (2) A gilli (a small wooden cylindrical peg, four to five inches long, tapered at both ends).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Game identified: Gilli Danda 1 Mark
Two equipment pieces: danda (long stick) and gilli (tapered peg) 1 Mark
Q2 According to the verses, what emotions and atmosphere do the players experience while playing Gilli Danda? Let us Think • Comprehension 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
The players experience immense exhilaration, freedom, laughter, and camaraderie. Playing under open skies fills their hearts with merry joy and healthy, energetic competition.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Joy, laughter, and high energy identified 1 Mark
Sense of freedom and open-air camaraderie 1 Mark
Q3 Explain what happens mechanically when the danda strikes the tapered tip of the gilli. Let us Think • Comprehension 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
When the player strikes one of the tapered, pointed ends of the gilli lying on the ground with the danda, it flips abruptly into the air. While the gilli is spinning airborne, the player quickly swings the danda to strike it with full force, sending it flying across the field.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Tapping the tapered end flips the gilli into the air 1.5 Marks
Second mid-air strike sends it flying forward across the field 1.5 Marks

Line 2 quoted accurately 1 Mark

Q6 Which specific vocabulary words in the poem express happiness and joy? Let us Think • Comprehension 2 Marks

The poem employs the expressive words 'joy' and 'merry' (as well as 'fun') to signify pure happiness and delight among the children.

Identification of 'merry' 1 Mark
Q7 Why do outdoor traditional games contribute more to a child's holistic health than indoor mobile gaming? Let us Think • Think & Discuss 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Outdoor games like Gilli Danda involve full-body movement, sprinting, bending, and sharp hand-eye coordination that strengthen bones and cardiovascular fitness. Furthermore, playing face-to-face teaches patience, team communication, and managing disappointments, whereas screen gaming fosters sedentary isolation and eye strain.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme

Q10 Write a clear, numbered 4-point guide on 'How to Play Gilli Danda Safely': Let us Write • Rulebook Writing 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Official Safety Rules for Gilli Danda:
  1. Select an Open Field: Always play in large grassy grounds or empty public parks, never in congested narrow residential alleys with glass windows.
  2. Clear Fielders' Perimeter: Fielders must stand at a safe distance (at least 15 meters away) in front of the striker, keeping their eyes focused on the airborne gilli.
  3. Check Equipment Quality: Ensure the wooden danda has no sharp splinters and the gilli ends are smooth to avoid skin cuts.
  4. Turn-by-Turn Striking: Only one striker swings the danda at any time; bystanders must remain strictly behind the batting mark.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Open space and field safety rules 2 Marks
Equipment integrity and turn discipline 2 Marks
Q11 Project Work: Research and document three indigenous traditional sports of India other than Gilli Danda. Let us Explore • Cultural Heritage 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
  • 1. Kabaddi: An ancient contact tag sport requiring breath control (chanting 'kabaddi'), lightning raid agility, and tactical defensive tackling.
  • 2. Kho-Kho: High-speed chase game where nine sitting players face alternate directions, requiring rapid sprinting, dodging, and teamwork.
  • 3. Mallakhamb: Traditional gymnastics performed on a vertical wooden teak pole, developing extraordinary core strength, balance, and flexibility.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Three traditional Indian sports accurately identified 1.5 Marks

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Reviving Traditional Sports & Digital Detox for Youth

Case Scenario: A public health survey revealed that 75% of primary students in an urban housing society spend over four hours daily on smartphones and tablets, leading to childhood obesity, poor social skills, and vitamin D deficiencies. The resident welfare association wants to launch an evening indigenous sports initiative.

Question: Draw on themes from 'Gilli Danda' to draft a 3-pillar action plan for the residential society to re-introduce traditional sports and encourage a healthy digital detox.

Three-Pillar Community Sports Revival Plan:
  1. Designate 'Vehicle-Free Play Hours': Block internal society lanes from car traffic every evening between 5:00 PM and 6:30 PM, creating safe, supervised zones for Gilli Danda, Kho-Kho, and Hopscotch.
  2. Grandparents' Traditional Sports Workshop: Invite elderly residents to teach children the authentic rules, wood-crafting tips, and tactics of indigenous games like Gilli Danda, building intergenerational warmth.
  3. Monthly Inter-Block Tournaments: Organize weekend mini-tournaments with handmade certificates, fruit baskets, and trophies to build pride and excitement around outdoor sports.
Rubric: 1.5 Marks for identifying screen addiction risks + 3.5 Marks for 3 feasible, vibrant community sports initiatives = 5 Marks

Chapter 8: The Decision of the Panchayat

Classic Indian folktale on truth, justice, rural jurisprudence & outsmarting deceit

📄 Open Standalone Chapter Page (22 Questions) ↗
Chapter Highlights, Thematic Summary & Key Vocabulary
  • Themes of ethical honesty, village community justice (Panchayati Raj), and exposing crafty loopholes.
  • A farmer purchases a well to irrigate his fields, but the dishonest neighbor claims he sold only the well, not the water.
  • The Village Panchayat's witty, brilliant verdict: if you own the water, pay rent for storing it in the farmer's well or empty it immediately!
  • Grammar: prepositions of place and direction, and deriving abstract nouns using suffixes.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Comprehension (22 Solved Questions)
Q1 Why did the hardworking farmer buy the well from his neighbor? Let us Think • Comprehension 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
The farmer had purchased an adjoining agricultural field and needed a dependable, perennial source of freshwater to irrigate his growing crops and sustain his family.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Purchased adjoining farmland 1 Mark
Needed reliable water for crop irrigation 1 Mark
Q2 Why did the farmer become deeply distressed the day after completing the purchase? Let us Think • Comprehension 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
When the farmer went to draw water the following morning, the cunning neighbor stopped him aggressively, claiming deceitfully that he had sold only the physical well structure, but not the water contained inside it.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Neighbor stopping farmer from drawing water 1 Mark
Cunning claim: sold well structure, not the water 1 Mark
Q3 How did the Village Panchayat use clever logical reasoning to resolve the dispute? Let us Think • Comprehension 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
The Panchayat elders used the neighbor's own dishonest logic against him. They declared that since the physical well now lawfully belonged to the farmer, the neighbor had no legal right to store his water inside the farmer's property. Therefore, the neighbor must either pay daily rent to the farmer for storing his water, or remove all his water immediately!
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Panchayat accepting that the well belongs to farmer 1 Mark
Counter-argument: neighbor cannot store water in farmer's property 1 Mark
Ultimatum: pay storage rent or remove water immediately 1 Mark
Q4 What was the final judgment delivered by the Panchayat, and what was its effect on the neighbor? Let us Think • Comprehension 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
The Panchayat ordered the neighbor to either vacate his water from the well at once without spilling a drop onto the farmer's land, or surrender full water rights to the farmer. Realizing his deceit had been completely foiled by superior wisdom, the neighbor hung his head in shame and conceded unconditional access to the farmer.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Panchayat's binding ultimatum delivered 1.5 Marks
Neighbor conceding defeat in shame, full rights given to farmer 1.5 Marks
Q5 Do you agree that the decision of the Panchayat was fair, just, and morally sound? Why? Let us Think • Think & Discuss 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Yes, the decision was exemplary. It upheld justice by exposing the neighbor's bad-faith technicality. Selling a well naturally implies selling access to its water. By turning the trickster's own words back upon him, the elders protected the honest farmer without violence or prolonged litigation.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Affirmation of justice and fairness 1.5 Marks
Insight on dismantling dishonest technicalities with wit 1.5 Marks
Q6 What moral values does this traditional story teach regarding business dealings and community life? Let us Think • Think & Discuss 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
The story teaches that integrity and honesty are paramount in contracts. Attempting to exploit loopholes to cheat others ultimately leads to public humiliation. True justice requires wisdom and courageous community arbitration where the voice of truth triumphs over greed.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Integrity in agreements / contracts 1.5 Marks
Truth prevailing over greed and trickery 1.5 Marks
Q7 Match the following vocabulary words from the story with their contextual definitions: Let us Learn • Vocabulary 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
  • Prospered: Became successful, wealthy, and thriving.
  • Cunning: Clever in a deceitful, dishonest, or crafty manner.
  • Summon: To officially call upon someone to appear before a council or court.
  • Judgment: An official, binding decision delivered by an authorized panel or judge.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
All 4 vocabulary definitions matched correctly 3 Marks

All 4 abstract nouns derived correctly 3 Marks
Q10 Write a diary entry (60–70 words) from the perspective of the relieved farmer after winning the Panchayat case. Let us Write • Diary Entry 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Dear Diary,
What a day of relief and gratitude! When my neighbor refused me water from the very well I had bought with my life savings, my heart had sunk. But today, under the shade of the village banyan tree, the Panchayat proved that truth cannot be silenced by cunning tricks. Their sharp reasoning outsmarted his deceit in minutes. Tonight, my fields will drink fresh water, and my children will sleep peacefully. God bless our wise elders!
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Appropriate diary format and sincere emotional tone 2 Marks

Q11 Project Work: Describe the structure of a Village Gram Panchayat in India and its role in resolving local disputes. Let us Explore • Civics & Panchayati Raj 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Panchayati Raj Grassroots Governance:
  • Gram Sabha: The general body comprising all adult voting residents of the village.
  • Gram Panchayat: The elected executive council headed by the Sarpanch (village head) and ward members (Panchs).
  • Dispute Resolution: Panchayats resolve family, property, and boundary disputes locally through mediation, avoiding costly police and court litigation while preserving community harmony.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Gram Sabha and Gram Panchayat structure defined 1.5 Marks
Local dispute resolution function explained 1.5 Marks

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Consumer Rights, Contractual Integrity & Legal Loopholes

Case Scenario: A shopkeeper sells a brand-new desktop computer to a student. When the student opens the package at home, the power cable and keyboard are missing. When confronted, the shopkeeper cunningly argues: 'The bill says computer screen and CPU box; accessories require an additional fee.'

Question: Drawing a parallel to the trickery in 'The Decision of the Panchayat', identify the unfair trade practice and explain how consumer protection forums deliver justice in such cases.

Legal & Ethical Resolution under Consumer Protection:
  1. Identification of Deceit: Just as the neighbor tried to sell an empty well while denying its essential water, the shopkeeper is engaging in an 'Unfair Trade Practice' by selling an unusable product that cannot operate without its essential basic power cable.
  2. Doctrine of Implied Fitness: In commercial law, goods must be fit for their intended purpose. A computer sold without a power cord violates basic contractual good faith.
  3. Consumer Forum Remedy: The student can file a complaint with the National Consumer Helpline or District Consumer Commission. The forum will order the retailer to immediately supply all missing operational accessories and pay compensation for harassment.
Rubric: 1.5 Marks for connecting well/water deceit to modern consumer rights + 3.5 Marks for legal doctrine of fitness and redressal mechanism = 5 Marks

Chapter 9: Vocation

Rabindranath Tagore's poetic masterpiece exploring childhood imagination, routine & dignity of labour

📄 Open Standalone Chapter Page (22 Questions) ↗
Chapter Highlights, Thematic Summary & Key Vocabulary
  • Themes of childhood innocence, the allure of freedom, occupational empathy, and the dignity of labour.
  • The child's daily schedule contrasts with the unrestricted freedom of the hawker, the gardener, and the night watchman.
  • Vivid poetic imagery: the gong striking ten, the giant street lamp with a red eye, chasing shadows with a lantern.
  • Dignity of labour: honoring honest everyday community workers without bias or condescension.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Comprehension (22 Solved Questions)
Q1 Who is the speaker in Rabindranath Tagore's poem 'Vocation'? Let us Think • Comprehension 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
The speaker is a young, observant schoolboy who shares his thoughts and longings as he follows his daily routine from morning until bedtime.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Identification of the young schoolboy 1 Mark
Child perspective navigating daily routine 1 Mark
Q2 Why does the speaker yearn to become a bangle-selling hawker? Let us Think • Comprehension 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
The speaker is captivated by the hawker's absolute freedom: the hawker has no fixed road he must travel, no compulsory destination, no strict clock telling him when to go home, and nobody scolding or hurrying him.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Absence of fixed routes and strict schedules 1 Mark
Freedom from being hurried or scolded 1 Mark
Q3 What specific activities of the gardener appeal deeply to the child? Let us Think • Comprehension 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
The child is fascinated that the gardener can dig the damp soil with his spade freely, soil his clothes with mud and dust, and get soaked in the rain or baked under the hot sun without any adult intervening, scolding him, or stopping him.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Freedom to dig soil with spade 1 Mark
Getting clothes muddy without scolding 1 Mark
Enduring sun and rain without restriction 1 Mark
Q4 What striking visual metaphor does the poet use to describe the street lamp at night? Let us Think • Comprehension 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
The poet compares the solitary glowing street lamp to an enormous giant standing tall in the dark lane with a single shining red eye on its head.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Metaphor of a giant 1 Mark
With one red eye on its head 1 Mark
Q5 Chart the chronological daily schedule of the child speaker as described in the poem: Let us Think • Comprehension 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
  • 10:00 AM: The temple/clock tower gong strikes ten, and the child walks down the narrow lane to school, encountering the hawker crying "Bangles, crystal bangles!"
  • 4:00 PM: The child returns home from school and peers through the open garden gate, watching the gardener digging the earth.
  • Late Evening (Bedtime): Mother sends the child to bed; gazing through his bedroom window, he watches the lonely night watchman walking up and down with his lantern.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
10 AM morning encounter with hawker 1 Mark
4 PM afternoon return watching gardener 1 Mark
Bedtime night view of watchman 1 Mark
Q6 Why does the child romanticize the vocations of the hawker, gardener, and watchman, while overlooking their hardships? Let us Think • Think & Discuss 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
The child feels constrained by strict adult-imposed rules (fixed school hours, homework, staying clean, mandatory bedtimes). In his innocent yearning for independence, he sees only their freedom of movement, unaware of the hawker's financial insecurity, the gardener's exhausting physical fatigue, or the watchman's chilly, perilous night shifts.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Contrast between child's rigid routine and perceived freedom 1.5 Marks
Insight into underlying economic and physical hardships 1.5 Marks

Q11 Explain Mahatma Gandhi's philosophy of 'Bread Labour' and why every occupation deserves equal dignity and respect. Let us Explore • Social Studies 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Dignity of Labour & Bread Labour:
Mahatma Gandhi championed the principle that every human being should perform honest physical labor to earn their livelihood. He emphasized that no work is 'lowly' or 'inferior'—whether one is a philosopher, engineer, farmer, or sanitation worker, all work that supports life is sacred and honorable. A civilized nation treats manual workers with the same dignity, fair wages, and courtesy as office professionals.

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Workplace Empathy, Child Labor Awareness & Social Responsibility

Case Scenario: While walking back from school, 10-year-old Meera sees a young boy her own age working at a roadside tea stall, washing greasy tumblers and serving hot glasses in the afternoon heat. Unlike Tagore's poetic speaker who romantically wished to be a hawker, Meera realizes the boy is missing school due to family poverty.

Question: Contrast the child speaker's romanticized viewpoint in 'Vocation' with Meera's real-world realization regarding child labor. Propose three civic actions to uphold children's Right to Education (RTE).

Critical Contrast & Child Rights Action:
  1. Poetic Fantasy vs. Grim Reality: Tagore's speaker views street vocations through an innocent prism of freedom from homework and bedtimes. Meera observes the painful socio-economic reality of child labor, where young children are robbed of their fundamental right to play, learn, and grow safely.
  2. Report to Childline (1098): Citizens should report child labor instances to the national toll-free helpline 1098 or District Child Protection Units for immediate rehabilitation.
  3. Enrollment in RTE Government Schools: Connect the child's family with local Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan centers that provide free education, midday meals, textbooks, and uniforms under the Right to Education Act.
  4. Ethical Consumer Boycott: Refuse to patronize commercial establishments that illegally employ underage children.
Rubric: 1.5 Marks for contrasting romanticized freedom with socio-economic reality + 3.5 Marks for 3 actionable child-rights protection measures = 5 Marks

Chapter 10: Glass Bangles

Inspirational narrative on traditional Indian handicrafts, creative innovation & community upliftment

📄 Open Standalone Chapter Page (22 Questions) ↗
Chapter Highlights, Thematic Summary & Key Vocabulary
  • Themes of traditional artisanal craftsmanship, family entrepreneurship, and rural innovation.
  • The glassmaking heritage of Firozabad, Uttar Pradesh: turning recycled glass and sand into vibrant jewelry.
  • Ananya's artistic innovation: blending modern geometric and floral motifs with ancient furnace techniques.
  • The ripple effect: increased business uplifts local artisans, packers, traders, and women workers.
  • Grammar: compound words, process writing, and descriptive vocabulary.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Comprehension (22 Solved Questions)
Q1 Describe the traditional step-by-step process of making glass bangles inside Ravi's workshop. Let us Think • Comprehension 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
In Ravi's workshop, raw glass and recycled colorful shards are first placed inside high-temperature clay furnaces until they melt into glowing, malleable red liquid. Artisans dip long iron rods into the molten glass, wind the threads around rotating spiraled metal mandrels to form coils, cut them into individual rings with diamond cutters, and seamlessly solder the joints over narrow flame torches.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Melting raw/recycled glass in clay furnaces 1 Mark
Drawing molten threads onto rotating mandrels to form coils 1 Mark
Cutting and flame-soldering individual circular joints 1 Mark
Q2 Who was Ananya, and how did her creative artistic vision transform her father's traditional craft? Let us Think • Comprehension 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Ananya was Ravi's young, observant daughter. Recognizing that younger generations desired contemporary styles, she designed fresh floral motifs, delicate geometric patterns, and elegant pastel color combinations. By blending traditional glass craftsmanship with modern aesthetics, she created bangles that appealed to modern markets.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Ananya identified as Ravi's daughter 1 Mark
Introduction of modern geometric & floral motifs 1 Mark
Blending ancient technique with contemporary aesthetic 1 Mark
Q3 How did the booming market success of the new bangle designs uplift the broader local community? Let us Think • Comprehension 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
The huge surge in demand created extensive employment across the entire village: more local craftsmen were hired at fair wages to mold bangles; neighborhood women gained income decorating and packaging them in padded gift boxes; and local transport drivers prospered shipping cartons to city festival markets for Diwali.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Increased employment for local artisans with fair wages 1 Mark
Empowerment and income for neighborhood packaging women 1 Mark
Economic stimulus for local logistics and transport drivers 1 Mark

✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:

Creative contemporary design proposals 1.5 Marks
Eco-friendly packaging and digital storytelling strategy 1.5 Marks

Q8 Write a 4-step instructional guide on 'How to Safely Make a Decorative Paper Lantern for Festivals': Let us Write • Process Writing 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Crafting a Festive Paper Lantern:
  1. Select & Fold Paper: Take a colorful rectangular sheet of craft paper and fold it in half lengthwise.
  2. Make Parallel Slits: Use safety scissors to cut parallel slits along the folded edge, stopping one inch before the outer margins.
  3. Roll into Cylinder: Unfold the sheet, curve it into a circular cylinder so the slits flare outward gracefully, and staple the edges together.
  4. Attach Handle & Hanger: Glue a contrasting paper strip to the top rim as a handle, and hang it near a doorway with fairy lights.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Clear 4-step chronological craft process 2 Marks
Action verbs, safety precautions, and precise instructions 2 Marks
Q9 Research & Fact Card: Why is the city of Firozabad in Uttar Pradesh celebrated across the world as 'The Bangle City'? Let us Explore • Cultural Geography 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Firozabad: The Glass Heritage Capital of India:
  • Centuries-Old History: Glassmaking in Firozabad dates back over 200 years, producing glassware, chandeliers, and bangles for Mughal and Indian royal courts.
  • Global Hub: It is the largest producer of glass bangles in the world, employing hundreds of thousands of traditional glassblowers and artisans.
  • Cultural Symbolism: Glass bangles are an auspicious symbol of matrimonial happiness, prosperity, and joy celebrated across Indian festivals like Karwa Chauth, Teej, and Diwali.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Historical heritage of Firozabad explained 1.5 Marks
Economic scale and cultural significance of bangles 1.5 Marks

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Handloom & Handicraft Revitalisation in the Digital Age

Case Scenario: Many young members of traditional artisan families across India are abandoning ancestral crafts like handloom weaving, pottery, and brass sculpting to take up unfulfilling low-wage urban labor, citing low income and exploitative middlemen in local bazaars.

Question: Drawing inspiration from Ananya's entrepreneurial success in 'Glass Bangles', formulate three innovative strategies that can empower traditional rural artisans to prosper in the digital era.

Three Strategies for Handicraft Revitalisation:
  1. Direct-to-Consumer (D2C) E-Commerce & Artisan Platforms: Establish village cooperative portals where artisans list their products directly on national and global e-commerce marketplaces (like ONDC, Etsy, and Amazon Karigar), bypassing predatory middlemen and retaining 90%+ of sales value.
  2. Design Mentorship & Design School Collaborations: Connect rural workshops with fashion and industrial design institutes (like NID and NIFT) to co-create modern lifestyle products (home decor, minimalist jewelry, tech sleeves) using traditional handmade techniques.
  3. Fair-Trade Artisan Storytelling: Attach a verifiable 'Handmade in India' tag and QR code to every product, sharing video stories of the specific artisan family who crafted it, appealing to ethical global consumers willing to pay premium prices.
Rubric: 1.5 Marks for identifying middleman exploitation and artisan abandonment + 3.5 Marks for 3 actionable digital/design/fair-trade business strategies = 5 Marks

Unit 1: Ice-cream Man & Wonderful Waste!

Summer joy poem by Rachel Field & Folk tale from Travancore (Kerala)

📄 Open Standalone Chapter Page (22 Questions) ↗
Chapter Highlights, Thematic Summary & Key Vocabulary
  • Poem 'Ice-cream Man': The summer arrival of the ice-cream cart bringing delightful cooling treats (vanilla, chocolate, strawberry) and chilled fizzy drinks; cart compared to a colourful flower bed.
  • Prose 'Wonderful Waste!': The Maharaja of Travancore commands a grand feast; enters the kitchen and strictly forbids discarding vegetable scraps.
  • The Culinary Invention of 'Avial': Slicing vegetable peels into long strips, boiling them with ground coconut, green chillies, garlic, beaten curd, and aromatic curry leaves.
  • Key Themes: Resourcefulness, zero-waste culinary ethics, sustainability, and creative problem solving.
  • Grammar & Phonics: Describing words, rhyming pairs, compound words, step-by-step recipe writing.

Q1 In which season is ice-cream most popular, and who feels joyful on seeing the Ice-cream Man? Reading is Fun • Poem (Ice-cream Man) 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Explanation:
Ice-cream is most popular during the blazing heat of the summer season. Children (and the speaker) feel immense joy and excitement upon spotting the Ice-cream Man wheeling his cool, colourful cart down the street.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Summer season identified 1 Mark
Children / speaker feel joyful excitement 1 Mark
Q2 What are the different flavours of ice-cream mentioned in the poem, and what else does the Ice-cream Man sell? Reading is Fun • Poem (Ice-cream Man) 3 Marks
